summary:
I found no work, up to 2026-10-01, that chooses among maximal quadratic-free (or other S-free) sets to get the best intersection cut for QCQPs. I checked the citation lists of six papers (Muñoz–Serrano 2022, Chmiela–Muñoz–Serrano 2023, Muñoz–Paat–Serrano 2025 and 2026, the 2025 monoidal-strengthening paper, Bienstock–Chen–Muñoz 2020) in Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and OpenCitations, and ran 28 web searches and arXiv queries. This is an unsuccessful search, not proof of novelty.

The audit changes the context of three results:

1. **Theorem 1 is close to known cut-generating-function results.**
   - Cornuéjols–Wolsey–Yıldız 2015 (Thm 1.1) and Conforti et al. 2015 (Thm 6.3) already give exact single-cut attainment of the corner bound under cone conditions.
   - Conforti et al. §6 contains the same failure mechanism as Proposition 2(a).
   - Theorem 1(2) can be derived from Kılınç-Karzan–Yang Cor. 3.12, an unrefereed author draft (revised 2017).
   - Theorem 1(4) survives. It covers the boundary case those strict conditions leave open; the Theorem 14 corner is such a case (exact check).
2. **Proposition A (known result).** When the projected rays positively span R^k, the simplex conv{s̄, s̄ + (z_K/w_j)p_j} is S-free and attains z_K for every w ≥ 0. This holds on 0 of the 120 McCormick LP corners of the earlier experiments, so it has no direct effect on them.
3. **Orbit family.** Bienstock–Chen–Muñoz's sets (14a) are exactly the orbit sets {sym(F^T M) ⪰ 0} with F a rotation (Proposition B, proved and checked exactly). The sfree orbit is a 3-parameter extension. Bienstock–Chen–Muñoz also wrote (arXiv v7, p. 24) that their violation-based choice "may not translate to finding the deepest cut"; any paper must cite this.

Among the classical works, Eckstein–Nediak (Ann. Oper. Res. 2005) is the closest precedent: they pose a "deepest cut generation problem" over S-free sets, but for mixed-integer programs with distance-based depth. Glover 1973 and Konno 1976 define the same cut-strength ordering but have no selection theory for quadratic sets. Balas–Margot work on the complementary axis (fix the set, tighten the relaxation).

**Solver baseline.** Quadratic intersection cuts have been off by default since SCIP 8.0 and still are in 10.0.3. The published reason is cut density and no rule for when the cuts help, not cut weakness. The only published evaluation I could read is a root-node experiment (ZIB-Report 20-29: mean gap closed 0.56 → 0.62 on 587 MINLPLib instances), with no published branch-and-bound comparison.

results.claim: No paper found (to 2026-10-01) on choosing among maximal quadratic-free/S-free sets for cut strength or on best single intersection cuts for QCQP; all citers of the MS/MPS/Chmiela/monoidal/BCM papers (Semantic Scholar via WebFetch, OpenAlex, OpenCitations) address other questions.

Theorem 1(2) (supremum of single-cut bounds = z_K for w > 0, closed S) follows from Kilinc-Karzan-Yang draft Cor. 3.12 by choosing D_1 as minimal ray representatives in cl(B_2) and D_2 as the remaining rays; exact attainment under S - xbar in cone(R) is Cornuejols-Wolsey-Yildiz Thm 1.1.
results.location: note.md Section 4.4 Remark 4.4 (conditional on the unrefereed KY Cor. 3.12)

results.claim: Proposition A: if cone(P) = R^k (or S_k - sbar in cone(P)), the corner bound is attained by a single S-free set for every w >= 0 with 0 < z_K < infinity; the polytope sbar + P{lambda >= 0 : w^T lambda <= z_K} works when cone(P) = R^k. This is CCDLM Thm 6.3 / CWY Thm 1.1 specialized; not new.
cone(P) = R^3 holds in 0 of 47 (seed 11, 4x4) and 0 of 73 (seed 12, 6x8) McCormick LP corners of the sfree note Section 9.2, so Proposition A never applies there.

At the Theorem 14 corner, points of int S outside the cone accumulate at the unique minimizer t* (q(t*+eps n) = 18 eps(-60 eps - 11), cost of t* exactly z_K = 1), so Kilinc-Karzan-Yang's strict condition (iii) fails while Theorem 1(4) (grad q(t*)^T(sbar - t*) = 3/2 > 0) still gives attainment.

Proposition B: sym(G_t M) PSD with G_t a rotation iff cos t (a+d) - sin t (b-c) >= ||(b+c, a-d)||, i.e. BCM's maximal OPF sets (14a) are the orbit sets C_F with F in SO(2); for F^T = diag(2,1/2), C_F is neither a (14a) nor a (14b) set.
results.location: note.md Section 5.2; code/check_bcm_orbit.py (sympy identities True, 0/20000 random disagreements, exact witness M1/M2); logs/check_bcm_orbit.log

results.claim: BCM 2020 (arXiv v7, Lemma 24 and Remark, p. 24) explicitly flags that the violation-maximizing lambda 'may not translate to finding the deepest cut'; the selection question was posed but not solved before the sfree note.

Eckstein-Nediak (RUTCOR RRR 23-2003; Ann. Oper. Res. 139, 2005) formulate a deepest-cut generation problem over S-free sets for MIP (distance-based depth, finite Y, restricted parametrizations); this is the closest classical precedent and must be cited.

SCIP baseline: quadratic intersection cuts off by default since 8.0 and in 10.0.3 (DEFAULT_USEINTERCUTS FALSE, usestrengthening FALSE, usemonoidal TRUE, disabled in sub-SCIPs); stated reason is density and no rule for when they help; the only published evaluation found is root-node (ZIB 20-29 Section 5: mean gap closed 0.56 to 0.62 on 587 MINLPLib instances, 27 more root solves, no branch-and-bound comparison).

Revised novelty: Thm 1(1)-(3),(5), Lemma 3 known or derivable; Prop 2(a) same mechanism as CCDLM Section 6 variant of Ex. 6.1; Thm 1(4), Prop 2(b), Thm 4, Thm 8, the 3-parameter orbit, Lemma 10, Prop 12, Thm 11, Lemma 13, Thm 14, Prop 16 not found in prior work; Thm 5 hardness is a standard Motzkin-Straus reduction; Prop 9 an elementary instance of a known phenomenon.

corrections_to_earlier_notes: sfree note Theorem 1 Remark (ii) and Section 10.2: Theorem 1 is not just 'folklore closure'. CWY 2015 Thm 1.1 is a single-cut dominance theorem giving exact attainment when S - xbar is in cone(R); CCDLM Thm 6.3 does the same when cone(R) = R^k; Kilinc-Karzan-Yang (draft) imply Thm 1(2); Prop 2(a) must cite the CCDLM Section 6 variant of Example 6.1 (HAL p. 25).

sfree note Section 10.2: Eckstein-Nediak (Ann. Oper. Res. 139, 2005), who pose a deepest-cut generation problem over S-free sets for MIP, were missing; Glover 1973 and Konno 1976 were cited from memory and are now read (same coefficient-wise strength order, no set-selection theory for quadratic sets).

sfree note Section 10.1 / scout report Section 1.3: 'Porembski (JOGO 2001, 2004)' is wrong; 2004 is Operations Research 52(6) 942-953; cone adaptation is JOGO 24 (2002) 89-107, not 2004; JOGO 2001 pages differ between Crossref (109-132) and zbMATH (113-136).
sfree note Section 10.2: Balas-Margot is Math. Program. 137 (2013) 19-35; GICs fix the S-free set and tighten the relaxation (complementary axis), choosing cuts by an LP over a point-ray collection.

sfree note Sections 8 and 10.2: BCM's (14a) sets are exactly the orbit members with F in SO(2) (Proposition B); BCM v7 p. 24 already flags that the violation-maximizing lambda may not give the deepest cut; the novelty claim should be 'three-parameter extension of a known one-parameter family'.
Scout report Section 1.1: BCM theorem numbers (4.3, 4.7, 4.10, 4.15) are local-KB numbering; arXiv v7 numbering is Thm 15/Cor 16, Thm 19, Cor 25, Thm 27.

sfree note Section 10.1: the Semantic Scholar list for arXiv:1911.12341 now has 17 entries (one new survey); citers of Chmiela et al. (missed in September due to rate limits) contain no set-selection work.

Solver statements (sfree Sections 5, 9.4; PROGRAM.md): 'off by default' is correct, but the published reason is density and no rule for when the cuts help, and the only published evaluation is root-node gap closed in a development SCIP; there is no published branch-and-bound comparison.
open_questions: Is there a characterization of attainment in the equality case that covers both Theorem 1(4) and Kilinc-Karzan-Yang's strict conditions (is the tangent-ray case of Prop 2(b) the only obstruction for quadratics)?
Can the Eckstein-Nediak deepest-cut formulation (sets X(d) from supporting hyperplanes at points of S) yield z_K-attaining maximal sets for quadratic S beyond the orbit family?

Do the journal versions of Chmiela et al. (Math. Program. 197, 2023) and of the monoidal paper (Math. Program. B 210, 2025) contain branch-and-bound comparisons that change the solver baseline? This needs library access.
Does BCM's violation-maximizing lambda lose a factor against the best rotation member or the full orbit on implied-minor corners, as Prop 6 shows for quadratic constraints? (minor-sets stream)
solver_relevance: There is no direct solver impact. In SCIP 10.0.3, quadratic intersection cuts are off by default. The published reason is that the cuts are dense and there is no rule for deciding when they help, not that they are weak. The only published evaluation I could read is a root-node experiment, with no branch-and-bound comparison. A better choice of S-free set improves cut strength but does not address density, so it matters for solvers only if a selection rule changes the on/off trade-off in branch-and-bound; the scip-set-selection stream is testing that. Proposition A does not apply to any LP corner studied (0 of 120).
